- Exclude organic causes
	- Pain
	- Encephalopathy
	- Delirium

- Physical restraint
	- Last resort only
	- Used to facilitate rapidly effective pharmacological treatment
	- Must be performed by appropriately trained staff


- Most important initial action
	- Reduce child’s distress
	- Reduce behavioural escalation and risk of harm

- Assessment
	- Adverse childhood experiences
		- May alter flight-fight-freeze response
		- Child may appear calm in frozen/dissociated state

- Briefly exclude:
	- Focal neurology
	- Acute pain
	- Altered conscious state
	- Toxidrome

- time to perform comprehensive examination
	- Performed after distress reduced

- Management


	- Aims
		- Verbal and non-verbal de-escalation
			- First-line intervention
		- Treat underlying causes
		- Involve senior staff early
		- Consider Code Response
		- Debrief:
			- Child
			- Family
			- Staff

	- Environment
		- Private calm quiet room
		- Soft lighting
		- Eliminate agitation triggers
		- Family presence
			- Case-by-case basis
		- Remove dangerous items
		- Be aware of exits
		- Ensure staff safety

	- Child
		- Respect personal space
		- Consider individual needs
			- Language
			- Neurodevelopmental conditions
			- Cognitive ability
			- Trauma history
		- Age-appropriate strategies
			- Distraction techniques
			- Familiar toys
			- Communication aids
			- Comfort objects
		- Address physical needs
			- Analgesia
			- Food
			- Drink
		- Anticipate early escalation
		- Consider early mental health involvement
		- Offer collaborative sedation
			- Ask child to take oral medication where appropriate

	- Staff / Self
		- Ensure aligned team plan before approaching child
		- One staff member communicates with child/family
		- Introduce self
		- Emphasise collaboration
		- Minimise provocative behaviours/interventions
		- Use:
			- Concise language
			- Non-judgemental language
			- Calm voice
		- Communication principles
			- One idea at a time
			- Active listening
			- Focus on child’s goals
		- Allow child opportunity to regain emotional control
		- Set clear behavioural limits
		- Avoid bargaining
		- Offer clear choices
		- Negotiate realistic options
		- Maintain professionalism
			- Ignore insults
			- Ignore challenging questions

- Investigations
	- Not routine
	- Consider if excluding organic causes of altered conscious state

- Treatment

	- Main Principle
		- Safe calming environment without physical restraint is priority

	- Sedation
		- Consider oral or IM sedation only if:
			- De-escalation unsuccessful
			- Safety concerns present

	- Consent
		- Obtain consent wherever possible
			- Ideally child and/or guardians
		- Includes:
			- Sedation
			- Medical procedures
		- Common law
			- Young person may consent if they have capacity
		- Unsafe situations
			- No consent required if:
				- Danger to self
				- Danger to others
		- Clinicians should understand:
			- Duty of care
			- Relevant Mental Health Act
		- Child not requiring acute medical/psychiatric care
			- Should be discharged to safe environment
			- Avoid unnecessary chemical/physical restraint

	- Acute Behavioural Disturbance Medication Flowchart
		- Used when:
			- Non-pharmacological management ineffective

	- Post-Sedation Monitoring
		- Monitor in safe clinical environment
		- Assess for side effects
		- Avoid unnecessary waking/irritation
		- Consider local sedation assessment scale

		- Monitoring Based on Clinical State

			- Alert child
				- 30-minutely observations
				- For 2 hours post-sedation

			- Agitated child
				- Continuous clinical observation
				- Regular vital signs

			- Altered conscious state
				- 1:1 clinical support
				- Continuous pulse oximetry
				- Regular medical review

		- After medication
			- Perform:
				- Medical assessment
				- Mental health assessment
			- Guides ongoing management

- Code Response
	- Required if:
		- De-escalation unsuccessful
		- Safety concerns present
	- Requires appropriately trained team
	- Follow local guidelines

- Documentation

	- Include
		- Reasons for sedation
		- Medications used
			- Dose
			- Route
		- Interventions used
			- Non-pharmacological
			- Effective measures
			- Unsuccessful measures

	- Additional documentation may include
		- Code Response
		- Patient safety / incident reporting
		- Staff safety / OHS
		- Consent
		- Mental Health Act
		- Restraint Register (NSW)

- Defusing and Debriefing
	- Behavioural distress management may be highly stressful for staff
	- Critical incident stress debriefing encouraged
	- Support:
		- Child
		- Family
	- Goals
		- Maintain therapeutic relationship
		- Prevent future distress

- Consider Consultation with Local Paediatric Team When
	- Admission required for:
		- Medical cause of behavioural disturbance
		- Observation until drug toxicity resolves
	- Local mental health clinicians involved in ongoing care

- Consider Transfer When
	- Requires tertiary inpatient mental health facility
	- Requires ongoing specialist care
	- Sedation complications occur
	- Required care exceeds hospital capability
	- Paediatric transfer
		- Refer Retrieval Services

- Consider Discharge When
	- Behavioural distress reduced/resolved
	- Significant medical illness excluded/addressed
	- Significant psychiatric illness excluded/addressed
	- Underlying cause treated
	- Carers:
		- Capable
		- Willing to take child home
	- Consider crisis care if required
	- Clear follow-up plan in place
		- Medical
		- Mental health

- Parent Information
	- Challenging behaviour — school-aged children
	- Challenging behaviour — teenagers
	- Disruptive disorders in children

# **Medication Adverse Reaction Table**

| Medication | Respiratory Depression | Extra pyramidal reaction | Neuroleptic malignant syndrome | Paradoxical reactions | Management |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Benzodiazepines | ✔ | – | – | ✔\* | Airway support; Consider Flumazenil\*\* |
| Typical antipsychotics (Droperidol) | If used with opioids | ✔ | ✔ | – | Benztropine 0.02 mg/kg (max 1 mg) IV or IM; Repeat in 15 min if required |
| Atypical antipsychotics (Olanzapine, Quetiapine, Risperidone) | ✔ | ✔ (fewer) | ✔ | – | Benztropine 0.02 mg/kg (max 1mg) IV or IM for olanzapine-associated dystonic reactions; Repeat in 15 min if required |
| Ketamine | With rapid administration | – | – | – | Airway support |

\* Paradoxical reactions, such as increased agitation and Anxiety, may occur in children with autism or developmental delay  
\*\* Do not give to child taking frequent or long-term benzodiazepines or to a child who may have taken substances associated with causing seizures. Always involve senior staff
